original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Exact stationary edge-priced dirty fanout over arbitrary nonzero unital rings, including noncommutative rings, with heterogeneous unit target coefficients.
scope_change_reason: Extend the coefficient domain explicitly excluded by Ross Richardson PR3121. This is a scoped algebraic interface result rather than an R439 H2/K replacement.
bottleneck_link: A side result: complete stationary fanout tariffs survive composite and noncommutative coefficients without extra source calls. No actual physical tariff matrix or changed recursive moment is supplied.
stop_rule: Stop at the first proved ring extension with bounded exact corroboration. Do not pursue nonunit-demand optima or a physical supplier.
evidence: Written free-module dirt-cut argument and ordered coefficient construction; exact finite words and unrestricted two-row residue-ring shortest paths.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: For nonunit target coefficients, what additional ideal or factorization constraints replace the unit-demand forest optimum?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The explicit Z/4 two-row example has true optimum 4 rather than the unit formula value 3.
open_questions.first_step: Classify every two-row demand over Z/4 at a declared stationary price matrix using exact affine-state shortest paths, then seek a structural formula.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nonunit coefficients cannot always be transported by a unit ratio; no all-ring classification is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a named physical caller provide coefficient-independent complete tariffs for a profitable ring-valued fanout?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The theorem supplies an abstract tariff optimum, not a recursive supplier improvement.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one actual caller and charge coefficient application, source access, frames, target lifetimes and restoration before optimizing.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical tariff matrix, chronological caller, storage/precision bill or compatible outer transfer is supplied.
